question:
A mathematics group is investigating the determinant of a product of two square matrices. They select $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & 2\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$. One student proposes that the determinant of $AB$ can be predicted from the individual determinants without first multiplying the matrices. The group decides to calculate both sides independently and compare the results to verify the proposed property.

(a) Calculate $|A|$.

(b) Calculate $|B|$ and hence predict $|AB|$.

(c) Obtain the matrix $AB$.

(d) Evaluate $|AB|$ directly and verify the proposed determinant property.
explanation:
(a)
$$|A|=\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & 2\end{vmatrix}=2(2)-1(3)=1$$
Therefore, $|A|=1$.

(b)
$$|B|=\begin{vmatrix}1 & -1\\2 & 3\end{vmatrix}=1(3)-(-1)(2)=5$$
Using $|AB|=|A||B|$, the predicted value is
$$|AB|=(1)(5)=5$$

(c)
$$AB=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
$$AB=\begin{bmatrix}2+2 & -2+3\\3+4 & -3+6\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 1\\7 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$

(d)
$$|AB|=\begin{vmatrix}4 & 1\\7 & 3\end{vmatrix}=4(3)-1(7)=5$$
Also,
$$|A||B|=(1)(5)=5$$
Thus,
$$|AB|=|A||B|$$
The proposed property is verified for the given matrices.

options.D:
(a) $|A|=-1$
(b) $|B|=5$ and predicted $|AB|=-5$
(c) $AB=\begin{bmatrix}4&1\\7&3\end{bmatrix}$
(d) $|AB|=5$, so the determinant changes sign
